name: EDU360
description: 360-degree videos are increasingly used in immersive learning, enabling engaging educational experiences. Capturing and modeling viewing data enables personalized content delivery, with the viewport (the region viewed at any given time) serving as a key indicator of user attention. The head and eye movement trajectories captured from VR devices provide strong cues to predict viewports and estimate viewer Quality of Experience (QoE). Existing datasets largely focus on capturing head and eye tracking signals, yet they seldom examine how these behavioral patterns influence or correlate with subjective QoE. This paper presents EDU360, an open dataset of head and eye movement with associated subjective QoE ratings. Data was collected from 32 users who watched 11 educational 360-degree videos at 4K/8K resolution using a fully wireless Meta Quest Pro headset. Analysis indicates potential relationships between behavior and perceived QoE: lower QoE tends to be associated with more constrained visual exploration and more concentrated gaze behavior, whereas higher QoE appears to correspond to broader exploration and more evenly distributed visual attention. These findings demonstrate EDU360's potential to support adaptive, personalized educational VR systems driven by head and eye movement data.
